previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, COPD, diabetes, hypertension, and prior AAA repair was admitted for shortness of breath and a 5-pound weight gain over two weeks. Evaluation showed mild pulmonary vascular congestion on chest X-ray and an elevated BNP, suggesting a mild heart failure component, though the patient appeared euvolemic. He also reported worsening dyspnea, consistent with a COPD exacerbation. An echocardiogram revealed a new apical left ventricular thrombus, prompting initiation of anticoagulation with enoxaparin and warfarin. A CT scan showed increased ulceration in the aortic wall near the diaphragm, which was not acutely dangerous but required vascular follow-up. The patient was discharged home with increased furosemide and lisinopril, instructions to complete outpatient pulmonary function tests, and close monitoring of INR and weight.
